scenario.name: Genshin Impact Anti-Cheat Driver (mhyprot2.sys) Ransomware BYOVD (CVE-2020-36603)
scenario.overview: Imagine a live television and radio broadcast studio with a glowing red ON AIR sign, a soundproof control-room window, a sliding mixing console, and a rooftop signal dish. Slipping into the broadcast control room beside the soundproof glass window, an unlisted engineer patches a covert jumper cord straight into the live mixing console. In this real-world scenario, the intruder approaches the soundproof on air studio door disguised as a regular visitor, then bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the mixing console & roof satellite dish. The master control broadcast log spots an unscheduled auxiliary transmitter channel pulling signal off the mixing board and cuts the rogue patch. In this scenario (T1068, Genshin Impact Anti-Cheat Driver (mhyprot2.sys) Ransomware BYOVD (CVE-2020-36603)), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: dropping Standalone Signed mhyprot2.sys, then opening \\.\mhyprot2, then ring-0 ZwTerminateProcess Massacre via IOCTL. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering Dropping Standalone Signed mhyprot2.sys, then Opening \\.\mhyprot2, then Ring-0 ZwTerminateProcess Massacre via IOCTL, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection correlates Sysmon Event 6 with the documented host and network chain.

stages.title: Stage 1: Dropping Standalone Signed mhyprot2.sys on Enterprise Domain Controller
stages.subtitle: Privilege Escalation & Defense Evasion (T1068 - Exploitation for Privilege Escalation)
stages.description: Slipping into the broadcast control room beside the soundproof glass window, an unlisted engineer patches a covert jumper cord straight into the live mixing console. Specifically in Step 1, the intruder approaches the soundproof on air studio door disguised as a regular visitor while everyday visitors and the broadcast director go about their routine. After compromising a server via RDP or stolen domain credentials, the ransomware operator dropped C:\Users\Public\mhyprot2.sys (a 350KB 64-bit Windows kernel driver validly signed by miHoYo Co., Ltd. and countersigned by Microsoft in 2020) and registered it as a kernel driver service via sc.exe create mhyprot2 type= kernel (loading cleanly into Ring 0 without requiring the Genshin Impact game client to be installed on the machine). Consumer anti-cheat drivers are engineered with sweeping Ring-0 process and memory inspection capabilities to catch game cheats, making them prime targets for standalone BYOVD weaponization on enterprise servers. In the documented EventID 6 exchange from kill_svc.exe Ransomware Dropper to Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap, Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap responds with ACK 6 (confirming that the Stage 1: Dropping Standalone Signed mhyprot2.sys on Enterprise Domain Controller request succeeded on Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap and establishing the runtime state required for Step #2 Stage 2: Opening \.mhyprot2 & Initializing MT19937-64 Encryption Seed (IOCTL 0x80034000)). On the diagram, follow Step #1 / Link #1 (#1→ Stage 1: Dropping Standalone Signed mhyprot2.sys on Enterprise Domain Controller / ⇠#1 ACK 6) from Node ① (#1 kill_svc.exe Ransomware Dropper) to Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 IOCTL 0x81034000 Ring-0 AV Wipe & Lock).

stages.title: Stage 2: Opening \\.\mhyprot2 & Initializing MT19937-64 Encryption Seed (IOCTL 0x80034000)
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion (T1027 - Obfuscated IOCTL Payloads)
stages.description: As the red ON AIR sign lights up above the studio floor, the covert bridge silently mirrors every studio feed up to the spinning rooftop signal dish. Here in Step 2 inside the broadcast studio, the intruder approaches the soundproof on air studio door disguised as a regular visitor without disturbing the backup emergency transmitter. kill_svc.exe opened a handle to \\.\mhyprot2 and issued DeviceIoControl with IOCTL 0x80034000 (passing a 24-byte initialization structure that seeds the driver’s internal 64-bit Mersenne Twister MT19937-64 pseudo-random number generator, which mhyprot2.sys uses to XOR-decrypt all subsequent IOCTL request buffers and XOR-encrypt responses). Because researchers had previously reverse-engineered mhyprot2.sys’s MT19937-64 key derivation and published open-source PoCs on GitHub (evil-mhyprot-cli), ransomware developers copied the exact handshake routine directly into kill_svc.exe. In the documented EDR exchange from Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap to Signed Anti-Cheat Driver (mhyprot2.sys), Signed Anti-Cheat Driver (mhyprot2.sys) responds with ALERT T1027 (confirming that the Stage 2: Opening \.mhyprot2 & Initializing MT19937-64 Encryption Seed (IOCTL 0x80034000) request succeeded on Signed Anti-Cheat Driver (mhyprot2.sys) and establishing the runtime state required for Step #3 Stage 3: Ring-0 ZwTerminateProcess Massacre via IOCTL 0x81034000 & Mass Encryption). On the diagram, follow Step #2 / Link #2 (#2→ Stage 2: Opening \\.\mhyprot2 & Initializing MT19937-64 Encryption Seed (IOCTL 0x80034000) / ⇠#2 ALERT T1027) from Node ② (#2 Perimeter Firewall & NDR Tap) to Node ③ (#3 Signed Anti-Cheat Driver (mhyprot2.sys)), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 IOCTL 0x81034000 Ring-0 AV Wipe & Lock).

stages.title: Stage 3: Ring-0 ZwTerminateProcess Massacre via IOCTL 0x81034000 & Mass Encryption
stages.subtitle: Defense Evasion & Impact (T1562.001 / T1486)
stages.description: Outside the building, the intruder tunes in to every private studio channel in real time while the broadcast director hears zero static in the headphones. In this final step inside the broadcast studio, the intruder bypasses the normal inspection rule to reach the mixing console & roof satellite dish until the master control broadcast log catches the mismatch. Once the 0x80034000 handshake succeeded, kill_svc.exe enumerated running endpoint security processes (Ntrtscan.exe, TmCCSF.exe, uiWatchDog.exe, MsMpEng.exe), XOR-encrypted each target Process ID with the MT19937-64 stream, and invoked IOCTL 0x81034000 (CVE-2020-36603, which calls PsLookupProcessByProcessId and ZwTerminateProcess in Ring 0 to forcefully terminate any process regardless of PPL status), immediately followed by mass ransomware encryption across the Domain Controller’s shares. mhyprot2.sys also exposes IOCTL 0x81054000 and 0x81064000 for arbitrary kernel/process memory reads (MmCopyVirtualMemory), giving attackers both an EDR killer and a kernel memory reader in a single signed binary. Mechanically, this stage is complete only after [object Object] and [object Object] is observed as live runtime state (the concrete checkpoint proving the previous stage's output now drives the next action). On the diagram, follow Step #3 / Link #3 (#3→ Stage 3: Ring-0 ZwTerminateProcess Massacre via IOCTL 0x81034000 & Mass Encryption / ⇠#3 ACK 5) from Node ③ (#3 Signed Anti-Cheat Driver (mhyprot2.sys)) to Node ④ (#4 IOCTL 0x80034000 MT64 Handshake), monitored by Node ⑥ (#6 IOCTL 0x81034000 Ring-0 AV Wipe & Lock).
